rationale: Tests understanding of why RF follows only pharyngeal GABHS — the molecular mimicry mechanism — anchored at the block explaining M-protein cross-reactivity with cardiac tissue.
Tests recall of Jones criteria classification — distinguishing major from minor criteria — anchored at the block presenting the CANES mnemonic and the full criteria table.
Tests the common misconception that a single normal ASO titre excludes recent GABHS — the 'ASO trap' described in this clinical pearl.
Tests understanding of the acute vs subacute IE distinction and the organisms responsible — anchored at the block classifying IE by clinical course, valve type, and causative agents.
Tests application of Duke's criteria by distinguishing major from minor criteria — anchored at the block presenting the full Duke's classification with major and minor criteria.
Tests correct blood culture collection technique for IE — anchored at the block detailing the full collection protocol including aseptic technique, number of sets, and transport requirements.
Tests recall of the classic PUO definition — students frequently confuse the duration thresholds for fever versus investigation — anchored at the block presenting the Petersdorf & Beeson definition.

Tests recall of Salmonella Typhi's Vi antigen — its nature, function, and clinical applications in vaccination and carrier screening — anchored at the block classifying enteric fever pathogens and their key antigens.
Tests understanding of the sequential pathogenesis of enteric fever from ingestion to clinical disease — anchored at the block presenting the step-by-step pathogenesis.
Tests the clinically critical skill of selecting the right diagnostic test based on week of illness — anchored at the block presenting the week-wise test selection table.

Tests interpretation of Widal test results distinguishing active infection from past exposure in an endemic setting — anchored at the block presenting Widal interpretation patterns and endemic-area caveats.
Tests recall of the four mechanisms by which infections cause anaemia and their key pathogen examples — anchored at the block presenting the mechanism classification table.
Tests application of iron studies to distinguish anaemia of chronic infection from iron deficiency — anchored at the clinical pearl presenting the discriminating laboratory features table.
